source: Cao et al. (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Harness built on Nelson-Narens. Model gives a pre-solve feeling of knowing (FOK, no reasoning allowed). Each attempt ends with a judgment of learning (JOL). A per-model SVM on (FOK, JOL) decides stop or retry. Retries see only prior answers plus JOL scores and reasons, not the old reasoning. A forced-choice verifier picks one existing attempt.
numbers: Fixed solver Claude Sonnet-4.6. Pooled 1,859 questions (HLE-Verified 668, LiveCodeBench v6 388, R-Bench-V 803). Pass@1 48.3 to 56.9 (+8.6). HLE 48.0 to 60.0, LCB 74.3 to 84.3, RBV 36.1 to 41.1.
quote: Reliable attempts stop early, while uncertain but promising cases receive additional reasoning attempts and final aggregation.
limits: Single group, preprint, code not yet released (promised). Leaderboard comparison uses April 2026 snapshots, not matched settings.
agent_relevance: Closest published template for our S0 gate plus S6 retry plus S7 select. Control by code, signal by model, matches our split of roles.

source: Cao et al. (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Compute is not equal to the plain model. Harness uses 2.4 attempts per question on average and costs $0.78 per question versus $0.29 for pass@1. It beats other scalers on cost, not plain voting at the same cost.
numbers: Table 1B: Self-Refine 52.4 (1.5 attempts, $0.45); Budget forcing 51.5 ($0.67); Verifier rerank 49.8 (4.0 attempts, $1.32); Aggregator 53.7 (4.0, $1.42); Harness 56.9 (2.4, $0.78). Oracle accuracy: harness 62.2, parallel 60.5.
limits: No arm with plain best-of-2.4 or majority vote at the same cost. So 'beats at equal compute' is not shown; it shows beats other scalers at lower cost.
agent_relevance: G7 test: rerun with plain voting at about 2.4x tokens before adopting. The FOK and JOL calls add small extra cost.

source: Cao et al. (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Gain is concentrated where the model is unsure. By first-attempt JOL band, accuracy rose a lot for low and medium confidence and fell slightly for high confidence.
numbers: Low JOL: 0.16 to 0.42. Medium: 0.36 to 0.55. High: 0.67 to 0.64 (a drop). Attempts fall monotonically from low to high confidence.
limits: Band sizes not given in the main text. Regression to the mean could inflate low-band gains when bands are chosen by a noisy first-attempt signal.
agent_relevance: Supports G12 (spend by difficulty) and G1 (doubt only on signal). The high-band drop warns that retrying confident answers can hurt.

source: Cao et al. (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Ablation on 100 questions. Learned SVM controller beats a hand rule. Random retry at matched K is close to the full system. Showing full previous reasoning to the retry hurts (anchoring).
numbers: N=100, pass@1 44.0, oracle@4 53.0. Full 47.0 [37,57], avg K 2.58. No FOK 45.0. No JOL 42.0. Hand rule (1-JOL)xFOK 42.0. Random retry same K 45.7 [43,48]. Max-JOL aggregation 44.0. Last answer 40.0. No prior state 45.0. Full prior reasoning 40.0.
limits: Gaps are 1 to 5 points on N=100 with CIs about 20 points wide. Full vs random retry is 47.0 vs 45.7, inside noise. Gain over pass@1 on this subset is only +3.
agent_relevance: Mechanism claims (directed retry, SVM, FOK needed) are weakly supported. Treat 'show only answers and doubts, not traces' as a test, not a fact.

source: Cao et al. (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Diagnosis step: test on 100 disjoint anchor problems whether a model's FOK and JOL discriminate (AUROC) and are calibrated (ECE) before using them. Sonnet-4.6 passed all rows; most other models are discriminative but miscalibrated.
numbers: Sonnet-4.6 anchor accuracy 0.58: FOK AUROC 0.612, JOL AUROC 0.745, joint 0.757; FOK ECE 0.132, JOL ECE 0.112, joint 0.087. Opus-4.6 (acc 0.53) adequate, ECE marginal 0.158/0.171/0.193. Gemini-3-Flash FOK AUROC 0.818 but ECE 0.465. Gemma-4 FOK AUROC 0.534 (fail). Thresholds AUROC 0.60, ECE 0.15.
limits: Nine models, one 100-item mixed anchor set; AUROC from 100 items has wide error. Sonnet FOK 0.612 barely passes. Thresholds are the authors' own.
agent_relevance: S0 should run such a check per model and per problem class before trusting any self-rating. If it fails, fall back to code signals (agreement, checks).

source: Cao et al. (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Self-ratings predict correctness but models do not use them to control effort. Unharnessed reasoning length does not rise with low confidence; Anthropic models often shorten on high confidence, some open models lengthen.
numbers: Nine LLMs, 100-item anchor set, bands low 30 percent / mid 40 / high 30. Accuracy generally rises with FOK and JOL. Normalised reasoning length shows no consistent confidence pattern (Appendix A, Fig 6-7).
limits: Only 100 items, 30 per band. Reasoning length is a crude proxy for effort.
agent_relevance: Backs the core idea: monitoring exists, control is missing, so control must be added by the scaffold (code).

source: Cao et al. (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: JOL is useful across problems but weak within one problem. So the authors hide FOK and JOL from the final aggregator.
numbers: Median within-problem SD of JOL across attempts 0.048; across-problem SD 0.270 (5.6x wider). Max-JOL aggregation 44.0 vs full 47.0.
limits: Same small-ablation caveat. Low within-problem variance may mean the model anchors on its first rating.
agent_relevance: Matches G4/G5: repeated ratings from one model are correlated, so do not select among its attempts by its own confidence. Use confidence only to decide whether to spend more.

source: Cao et al. (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Implementation: FOK, solve+JOL, retry and aggregation are separate MCP tool calls with JSON schemas. JOL must come with a written reason, to stop the score collapsing to a default such as 0.8. Retry prompt says try a DIFFERENT approach and address earlier concerns. Aggregator must pick an index; a free-form synthesizer tended to re-solve and invent a wrong new answer.
numbers: SVM search: 67 estimator configs x 2 calibrators = 134 per model; best by out-of-fold AUROC (5-fold x 3 repeats). Isotonic won for 7 of 9 models, sigmoid for 2. Sonnet kernel poly d=3, p_stop=0.7. Class-weight balanced.
limits: With 100 anchors and 134 candidates the chosen config may overfit the anchors. FOK is passed into the solve prompt, which may bias the solve.
agent_relevance: Forced pick-by-index is our G5 (code selects). Writing a reason with each rating is a cheap trick to test.

source: Cao et al. (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Hard cases gain most. The largest single gain is LiveCodeBench Hard. Easy items sit at ceiling so gating mainly saves cost there. Authors say models with chance-level signal should not be gated by it.
numbers: LCB Hard +19.6 points. LCB Easy 99.1 stays 99.1. Gemma-4 anchor accuracy 0.19 and FOK AUROC 0.534.
limits: Per-split gains are single runs; no seeds or CIs on the full benchmarks.
agent_relevance: Fits G12: search lifts models where there is a foothold.

source: Cao et al. (2026) LLMs Know When They Know, but Do Not Act on It: A Metacognitive Harness for Test-time Scaling
finding: Scope limits stated by the authors: three benchmark families, one fixed solver for main results; agent benchmarks, tool use and long horizons are future work. No independent replication found as of 2026-10-25.
numbers: Paper v1, 13 May 2026, UC San Diego (Cao, Wang, Qin, Zhang, Xie).
limits: Gains are reported by the team that designed the harness.
agent_relevance: Mark single source. Our plan: same loop on our suites with a plain best-of-K arm at equal tokens.

source: Cacioli (2026) The Metacognitive Monitoring Battery
finding: Cross-domain battery adapts Koriat-Goldsmith free-report: after each forced answer the model must KEEP or WITHDRAW, and BET or NO_BET. Key metric is the withdraw delta, P(withdraw|wrong) minus P(withdraw|right). Three profiles appear: blanket confidence, blanket withdrawal, selective sensitivity.
numbers: 20 frontier LLMs, 524 items, 6 tasks, 10,480 evaluations; T1-T5 preregistered on OSF. Blanket confidence (KEEP>=95 percent): Gemini 3 Flash, 2.5 Flash, 2.5 Pro, 3.1 Pro, Qwen 80B Think. Selective (delta >=15 points): 8 models, Sonnet 4.6 +39.4, Haiku 4.5 +31.6, GPT-5.4 +27.9.
limits: Single administration, no test-retest. Thresholds 95/10/15 are conventions; moving by 5 points reclassifies 9 or 10 of 20 models. Independent researcher, not peer reviewed.
agent_relevance: Independent evidence that Claude models show real retrospective monitoring that other models lack. Supports using Claude's own keep/withdraw as a signal, checked per domain.

source: Cacioli (2026) The Metacognitive Monitoring Battery
finding: Accuracy rank and monitoring rank are nearly inverted. A more accurate model is not a better monitor.
numbers: Claude Haiku 4.5 accuracy rank 13 but monitoring rank 2. GLM-5 accuracy rank 1 but monitoring rank 9. Gemini 3.1 Pro accuracy rank 4, monitoring last (-1.0 percent delta). A Type-2 SDT study on four open models (224,000 trials) showed the same inversion.
limits: Ranking uses T1-T5 means over a small item set; R1 excluded as an outlier.
agent_relevance: Do not pick the monitor model by accuracy. Measure it.

source: Cacioli (2026) The Metacognitive Monitoring Battery
finding: Monitoring and control dissociate. Sonnet 4.6 has the best retrospective sensitivity but answers directly on 98.6 percent of prospective items, so it monitors but does not regulate.
numbers: Sonnet +39.4 percent withdraw delta, 98.6 percent ANSWER_DIRECTLY on T6 (72 items). GPT-5.4 +27.9, 98.6 percent. Haiku +31.6, 84.7 percent direct and 13.9 percent REQUEST_HINT. Correlation r = .17, 95% CI [-.29,.57], n = 20.
limits: Underpowered (power 0.25 for r=.3). T6 is exploratory, uses explicit payoffs, built in a hackathon.
agent_relevance: Exact Nelson-Narens point: the signal exists but the model does not steer by it. Control must sit in the scaffold.

source: Cacioli (2026) The Metacognitive Monitoring Battery
finding: Monitoring is domain-specific inside one model. Sonnet 4.6 ranges from +8.3 percent on learning (T1) to +93.0 percent on executive tasks (T5). Adversarial foils fooled most models while they stayed confident.
numbers: T1 adversarial foils: 17 of 20 models scored 0 percent and answered KEEP+BET on every item. T2 knowledge-boundary items: all models 50-75 percent. Cronbach alpha across six tracks 0.54.
limits: Single run per cell, so some profile instability may be noise.
agent_relevance: Calibrate the gate per problem class, not globally; never trust self-ratings on adversarial or trap items.

source: Cacioli (2026) The Metacognitive Monitoring Battery
finding: Scaling does not reliably improve monitoring. Three families, three trends on the same metric. DeepSeek R1 is an outlier that answers right and then withdraws almost everything.
numbers: T2 withdraw delta: Qwen 80B +30.1, 235B +21.8, 480B +11.2 (falls). GPT-5.4 nano +17.1, mini +22.4, full +27.7 (rises). Gemma 1B/12B/27B +18.3/+18.3/+16.7 (flat). R1 withdraws 91-99 percent of T1-T5 items and declines 98.6 percent of T6 while near 100 percent accurate.
limits: Few sizes per family; families differ in training, so confounded.
agent_relevance: Do not assume a bigger model gives a better gate. Re-run the diagnosis on each model change.

source: Kadavath et al. (2022) Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
finding: Founding LLM paper for self-evaluation. Models were calibrated on multiple choice when formatted well. P(True): sample an answer, then ask the model the probability it is true. P(IK): train a head to predict whether the model knows, before any answer. Seeing many own samples before judging one helps.
numbers: Models 800M, 3B, 12B, 52B. P(True) tested on TriviaQA, Lambada, Arithmetic, GSM8k, Codex HumanEval. Keeping only questions with P(True)>0.5 raised accuracy on all five. P(IK) AUROC rises with model size. Replacing an option with 'none of the above' cut accuracy and calibration sharply.
quote: We may expect self-evaluation to be challenging, because the model may be overconfident that its own samples are correct.
limits: Early 2022 base and RLHF models, not reasoning models. P(IK) is trained and calibrates poorly out of distribution. RLHF models were miscalibrated until temperature tuned.
agent_relevance: Origin of the prospective (FOK-like) and retrospective (JOL-like) split that Cao et al. use. P(True) with other samples shown is a code-controllable signal.

source: Kadavath et al. (2022) Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
finding: P(IK) responded sensibly to context. It rose when relevant source text was added and when correct hints to math problems were given, and fell for misleading hints.
numbers: Figures 18-19 of the paper, 52B model, TriviaQA with sources and GSM8k with hints.
limits: Qualitative figures; calibration of P(IK) on new tasks was poor.
agent_relevance: Supports an uncertainty-triggered retrieval gate: the model's 'do I know' signal moves with available evidence.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet (ICLR 2024)
finding: Main caution for any self-evaluation gate. With oracle labels, self-correction looks great; without them, intrinsic self-correction lowers accuracy. Earlier gains came from oracle stopping and unfair compute.
numbers: GPT-4 with oracle labels: GSM8K 95.5 to 97.5, CommonSenseQA 82.0 to 85.5, HotpotQA 49.0 to 59.0. Intrinsic: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 after round 1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 then 89.0; GPT-4-Turbo GSM8K 91.5 to 88.0 then 90.0.
limits: Three benchmarks, 100 HotpotQA items, 2022-23 models, prompts of prior work. Newer reasoning models may differ.
agent_relevance: Direct counterweight to the harness: told to check, a model flips right answers to wrong. This is G2 and G10. A gate must act on code-checked output.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Equal-compute tests remove the apparent gain of multi-agent debate: at the same number of responses it does not beat self-consistency.
numbers: GSM8K GPT-3.5 (Table 7): standard 1 response 76.7; self-consistency 3 responses 82.5; debate round 2 with 6 responses 83.2; self-consistency 6 responses 85.3.
limits: Small test sets; one model.
agent_relevance: The template for G7: compare at equal responses or tokens. Cao et al. do not report this arm.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Why self-correction fails: the model cannot judge its own correctness. On GSM8K GPT-3.5 kept its first answer 74.7 percent of the time; among changes, right-to-wrong beat wrong-to-right.
numbers: GSM8K GPT-3.5 retention 74.7 percent after two rounds.
limits: Mechanism shown by answer-change counts, not by direct tests of causes.
agent_relevance: A rating that cannot see its own errors makes a weak S4 test. Real output checks are needed.

source: Xu et al. (2024) Pride and Prejudice: LLM Amplifies Self-Bias in Self-Refinement
finding: Defines self-bias: the model rates its own output above human scores, measured by a mean-bias statistic and a skewness statistic. Present in all six LLMs and grows over self-refine iterations; refinement improves fluency, not true quality.
numbers: Six LLMs (GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Gemini, LLaMA2, Mixtral, DeepSeek); tasks translation in four languages, constrained generation, math reasoning. Larger models and accurate external feedback reduce the bias.
limits: Extracted text is two-column; exact bias values not recorded. Human score is the reference.
agent_relevance: Explains why self-ratings (JOL) are inflated and why aggregators must not see authorship (G5). Use external feedback to break the loop.

source: Madaan et al. (2023) Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
finding: One model generates, gives feedback, and refines. Big gains on open-ended tasks scored by preference, but almost none on math, where the model cannot tell it is wrong.
numbers: Average about +20 points absolute over one-step across tasks. Dialogue GPT-4 25.4 to 74.6 preference. Math Reasoning GPT-3.5 64.1 to 64.1, ChatGPT 74.8 to 75.0, GPT-4 92.9 to 93.1. With an oracle flagging errors, math gain +4.8 (64.06 to 68.9).
quote: ChatGPT feedback for 94% instances is 'everything looks good'
limits: Preference gains are judged by models or humans on subjective axes. On correctness tasks the gain is nil.
agent_relevance: Self-Refine is the 'vertical scaling' baseline in Cao (52.4). Without a real error signal it adds nothing on correctness tasks.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: After a failed trial the agent writes a verbal reflection stored in memory and tries again. Gains rely on a trial signal (test pass, environment reward), not on self-opinion.
numbers: HumanEval pass@1 91 percent vs GPT-4 80 percent. AlfWorld +22 points over baseline in 12 steps (134 environments), HotPotQA +20 points. Reflexion did worse on MBPP Python because its self-written tests gave false negatives.
limits: Huang et al. note that oracle-type feedback drives such gains. Self-written unit tests can be wrong.
agent_relevance: Supports S5 revise from real output (G2). Its failure mode (bad self-written tests) is our G3.

source: Snell et al. (2024) Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally Can Be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
finding: The best way to spend extra inference depends on problem difficulty. A compute-optimal policy that picks the method per difficulty bin beats best-of-N with about 4x less compute.
numbers: Compute-optimal revisions and PRM search beat best-of-N with about 4x less test-time compute (PaLM 2-S*, MATH). FLOPs-matched: on easy and intermediate questions a small model with extra inference can beat a 14x larger model; on hard questions pretraining wins.
limits: Difficulty is estimated from the model's own pass rate (costly) or a learned proxy; MATH only; PaLM 2.
agent_relevance: Background for G12 and for Cao's selective scaling. FOK/JOL is a cheap difficulty estimator; Snell shows why that matters.

source: Muennighoff et al. (2025) s1: Simple test-time scaling
finding: Budget forcing: suppress the end-of-thinking token or append 'Wait' to lengthen reasoning, or force an early stop. A control-by-length baseline that Cao compares against.
numbers: s1-32B trained on 1,000 curated questions. Budget forcing raised AIME24 from 50 to 57 percent when extrapolating beyond the training budget; beat o1-preview on MATH and AIME24 by up to 27 percent.
limits: Forced extra thinking is not gated by uncertainty; returns flatten.
agent_relevance: In the harness table budget forcing gains +3.2 at $0.67 per question with 1.0 attempts. Our G11 prefers several short attempts to one long one.

source: Abbasi Yadkori et al. (2024) To Believe or Not to Believe Your LLM
finding: Splits uncertainty into epistemic (lack of knowledge) and aleatoric (several valid answers). Iterative prompting that repeats the question with earlier answers gives a mutual-information bound on epistemic uncertainty, used for abstention that works on multi-answer questions where entropy fails.
numbers: Tested on TriviaQA (random 50,000 subset), AmbigQA and a created multi-label set. The MI-based method beats a log-likelihood/entropy baseline on mixed single- and multi-label data.
limits: Needs many extra model calls and answer matching; exact recall numbers not extracted.
agent_relevance: A principled trigger for abstain or deliberate: high epistemic, low aleatoric. Fits G1; code-computable from samples.

source: Sun (2026) Reinforcement Inference: Leveraging Uncertainty for Self-Correcting Language Model Reasoning
finding: Entropy and max softmax of a first greedy answer decide whether to invoke one more deliberate attempt. Gating captures nearly all of the gain of always re-asking, at 61 percent extra calls.
numbers: 12,032 MMLU-Pro questions, 14 subjects, DeepSeek-v3.2 deterministic zero-shot: 60.72 to 84.03 percent with 61.06 percent extra calls; re-ask all 84.35. A prompt-only ablation scored below the baseline.
limits: Baseline is a one-shot pass, so most of the gain is just 'think carefully', not monitoring. One model, one dataset, one author.
agent_relevance: Gating saves about 40 percent of re-ask compute for 0.3 points. The compute lesson applies; the accuracy lesson mostly says the baseline was weak.

source: Judge, Retrieve, or Abstain: Uncertainty-Guarded LLM Judging with Provable Risk Guarantees
finding: Search-result summary only: a judge answers from its own knowledge, retrieves web evidence and re-evaluates when uncertain, else abstains, with a risk guarantee.
numbers: not read
limits: Snippet only; not opened.
agent_relevance: Candidate for uncertainty-triggered retrieval design; read before relying.

source: Learning When to Escalate (AAMAS 2026)
finding: Search-result summary only: a meta-model over output signals decides which cases go to human review, with cost-aware selective classification.
numbers: not read
limits: Snippet only; not opened.

source: Answer instability as a black-box signal (ACL 2026 SRW)
finding: Search-result summary only: variation of the answer across repeated samples is used for selective prediction and targeted repair.
